question:
A photodiode is used in reverse bias with a $10\,\text{V}$ supply and a load resistor $R_L=68\,\text{k}\Omega$ in series. The output voltage $V_o$ is taken across $R_L$.

The photodiode current under illumination is approximately

$$I=I_d+I_{ph},$$

where the dark current $I_d=2\,\mu\text{A}$ and the photocurrent $I_{ph}$ depends on illumination.

Case 1: $I_{ph}=40\,\mu\text{A}$

Case 2: $I_{ph}=150\,\mu\text{A}$

Assume the diode remains in the linear reverse-bias region only as long as the reverse bias across it stays positive. (That is, $V_o$ cannot exceed the supply.)

Find $V_o$ in both cases and identify in which case the photodiode leaves the linear reverse-bias region.
